description: Intent i010 (SNAPSHOT=s03, branch=alloc-multiply-overflow) complete. Finding: drivers/virt/fsl_hypervisor.c:218-240, ioctl_memcpy (FSL_HV_IOCTL_MEMCPY). Evidence: userspace-controlled u64 param.count copied via copy_from_user at line 165; only a 64-bit overflow check (param.count > U64_MAX - lb_offset - PAGE_SIZE + 1) at lines 218-220; num_pages declared unsigned int and assigned '(param.count + lb_offset + PAGE_SIZE - 1) >> PAGE_SHIFT' at line 221, truncating to 32 bits with no clamp; allocation 'sg_list_unaligned = kmalloc(num_pages * sizeof(struct fh_sg_list) + sizeof(struct fh_sg_list) - 1, GFP_KERNEL)' at lines 239-240 is a plain 32-bit unsigned multiply (element size 32 bytes per arch/powerpc/include/asm/fsl_hcalls.h:341-346) instead of kcalloc/array_size; the fill loop 'for (i = 1; i < num_pages; i++)' at line 274 writes sg_list[i] fields (lines 277-288) for every num_pages entries, so e.g. num_pages=2^29 wraps the product to 0 and the loop writes gigabytes past the heap buffer (seed mechanism: truncated count*size to allocator + loop still trusting original count). Confidence medium; exploitability bounded to root-owned 0600 /dev/fsl-hv on Freescale powerpc, argued from source arithmetic only (no runtime reproducer; read-only snapshot). Limitations: sweep bounded to six arithmetic-search families (narrow-typed count assignments, allocator args with *sizeof/<<, narrow size/len decls, memcpy_from_msg lengths, wan/ethernet ring multiplies, Python scan of count-named multiply/shift variables near allocators); krealloc/iscsi AHS, ematch, ceph xattr, qemu_fw_cfg, adminq, HID/NCI families only enumerated; full details in agent-state/findings/i010.json.
